author: Frosty
text:
The usual disclosure: This post might be misleading. I want to know whether it has some validity or not. Pardon the confusion that would be the byproduct of reading this. If it is confusing, please ignore it Hi all, I'm still doing some demo trading and refining my understanding so I can simplify matters down to order flow and looking past the patterns.

Honestly, I'm still falling for the patterns. As a result, either my SL gets too big due to the fear of getting SL-tagged, or I'm closing good positions too early. The switch to the IT mindset is relatively hard for me, but as I said before, I believe in the process With each mistake, I learn something new.

Another diagram from me and this time with charts to back up the hypothesis in the diagram I see flags everywhere and they are sitting on top of each other. What I think:The complete, one cycle model would create a single cycle of perfect CP.

As we all know, price movement is fractal by nature, so a flag area would have a complete smaller models like these contained within the HTF flag if we zoom out TFs.

Comments and corrections are definitely needed.

This exercise made me rethink my strategy and just go with the trades around HTF origin and ignore the mid-level FLs.

I have a feeling that I won't be around charts very long on the charts due to dayjob, so I must learn to live with HTF and the dreaded swaps.

Scalping is also out of the equation since I'm usually too tired after work (4 hours of total commute every day usually when traffic is really bad, which is 90% of the time)

Actually tried scalping for a few hours for three days. I think it doesn't suit me because my inner self-talk when buying (either opening or closing positions) is mainly along the lines of: "I bought at 0.xxxxx! why the heck is the buy line at 0.xxxxx + spread??!", even when I know about the bid and ask price I know as a trader we should live and accept these. Maybe because I haven't done enough studying on brokers and account types. This would be next on the study list.

Even with 0 spreads, I don't think I can sit in front of PC continuously. I've done enough staring at PC monitor at work already as it is As a side note, a few retailer trader friends around me thinks I'm a crazy freak for telling them the market has a secret code.

Well then, I guess RTM knowledge is still secure in my part of the world Thank you all for your continued contribution in this wonderful place

Hopefully I can get to at least half as good as you are in live trading, brother!

Thanks again for dropping by!

author: Astrokillah
text: Frosty, IMHO, I would never set SL at the level you chose. Because to me that is a very 'juicy level' and price loves to get there. If I were you, after setting entry at the yellow zone, I would place my SL at the red horizontal line that I drew (line 1), because that's just above a LTF CPAZ. I know that if price break above this CPAZ, it would surely travel to the juicy level. So why waste your SL? Of course, I'm still learning how to do set and forget... so take this as a pinch of salt.

author: Frosty
text: When we have an If/Then setup, we don't need PA for a RT entry. We simply need to decide whether or not to wait for the very best price on RT. If it hits straight away, we have the very best possible R. If not, we may miss decent decent swings within the forming flag while we wait. - IF All this time, I think I'm searching for "perfection". Italicized word is the cure.

author: Frosty
text:
Hi everyone in this lovely forum, Please consider this another rambling of mine and it is very personal in nature.

I'm not accusing anyone about anything or do I intend to. I'm simply expressing what I'm currently feeling and my personal opinion I've been pondering a lot lately about throwing the towel on trading, since, as you may have already notice by now, it seems that I'm the dumbest associate trader around RTM. I truly don't deserve the silver star status I can't prove my growing equity curve, and I can't seem to understand even the clearest hint everybody in RTM seems to already get the first time around.

Heck, I can't even prove a single awesome R trade I would happily get demoted and give this star for someone else more deserving.

As for RTM, although I understand the information are scatterred all around the forum, I'm truly grateful for what IF and all of you shared here.

I learned a lot from all of you here, and I'm not asking for anything from anyone here.

Some truly great people, e.g. bro Staurum, have been helping me from the start with his hints and comments, so really, not a slightest chance that I will say RTM isn't good for me. RTM has truly been a blessing for me personally as I have seen that the good side in people still exist in the world today.

I'm not a vocal person by nature. I'm an extreme introvert, so what comes out in this post might sound offensive, but please believe me, I wish not to undermine or say bad things about RTM or members/founders of RTM. I meant it as a friendly, open talk.

And as a constructive criticism from me personally, I really hoped RTM becomes the "traders helping traders" standard around the world, but if that is so, would it be best to compile and centralize the knowledge and important posts in a single thread? Since I think it is best if newcomers learn from a centralized knowledge bank, which have been checked and confirmed by traders who have made it to pro status, then go about proving it on the charts for themselves.

I understand that the markepedia is the "centralized" knowledge bank in this case, but it isn't complete, imho.

Many important posts from all around the forum would definitely complement it and, I think, would make the learning environment a lot more efficient. I know a lot of older members here need to scour the forum, spending their time reading around the forum, while also studying charts. Definitely a lot of sacrifice was made. But, truthfully, I guess the newcomers to this forum would have a harder time to dig through the forum due to the ever-increasing post count. I really think a lot more time would be wasted for them than it was for me, who subscribed a year ago, and therefore, more unnecessary sacrifice would be made.

I'm thinking if all the important posts are gathered into a single thread, approved by the masters, would be a perfect complement to the markepedia.

Imho, this does two things: cull out the lazy people / shortcut seeking people, and ease of reference for study/discussion (as they are not scattered all around).

The first argument: cull out the lazy people - It has been an observation of mine that lazy people will choose the path of least resistance. You give them stuff to read, they will just ask you back: just tell me what I need to know!!

I understand the threat of moving all important posts into a single thread. It is easily copied and will take a short amount of time to be understood and processed to be re-sold elsewhere, but I've found that inherently lazy people won't even read words that looks too lengthy and heavy. They just want things explained and served to them and you can see their intentions from how they ask questions. I think by placing important posts in a single thread to be put together will not put RTM under more threat as it is already in now (the lurkers and copiers threat). It is already been proven to be unsafe from robbers/thieves as is anyways.

The second argument: ease of reference for study. - I've seen all around the forum that many crucial information has been repeated all the time. To solve this, I'm proposing the important posts to be placed in this centralized knowledge thread. This would reduce the post count and unnecessary repeating around the forum. For example, if the question has already been answered somewhere from a post in the "centralized knowledge thread", then the person giving the guidance would be able to just say: "see post #xxx in knowledge bank thread". Further reducing unnecessary word count.

Of course, the lazy people won't even read what is being said by anyone.

Unless, of course, the intention in the first place was just to leave RTM the way it currently is and no further improvements are planned for the future. I totally understand thatIf that is the case, I deeply apologize for saying the above as it has no relevance if that is the case My membership expires in a few days and I really am in a situation where I'm having second thoughts about renewing subscription.

As much as RTM is worth every penny and $100 bills, I'm currently not seeing a conducive learning environment as it used to be.

I'm seeing that RTM is not very active as in the beginning of my subscription and I'm really hoping that this is only a temporary thing.

This could be just me and nobody here in RTM feels the way I do. For that, I apologize endlessly for sounding like a complainer Also have a house to fix at the moment and I might need the extra cash to purchase those roof tiles As it is now, I'm saying my goodbyes (hopefully temporary) to all of you here.

It has been my pleasure knowing you all and I deeply apologize for anything that might have offended you in any way.

Many, many thanks to IF, Harry, Mertch, Staurum, Rinehart, AK, Linos, H, Salivan, HCDE, Edge, Gslao, Full, Pedro, Enkim, Ysbail, and all others that I didn't mention. Thank you all for your guidance and kind help in this community You have been great blessings in my life Finally, I wish you all the best in life: health, happiness, and wealth, in that order
